html:
The Museum of Islamic Art in Doha opened in 2008 on its own island off the Corniche. Its building was designed by the architect I. M. Pei, who was in his nineties and drew on old mosques of Cairo.

It holds one of the great collections of Islamic art: ceramics, metalwork, carpets, manuscripts and glass from Spain to India across fourteen centuries. It is run by Qatar Museums, chaired by a daughter of Emir Hamad.

The museum began a building race in the Gulf, followed by the Louvre Abu Dhabi and the National Museum of Qatar. Like the World Cup, it was meant to make Qatar known for more than gas.
